docs.title: DUSTY ROADS EXPANDED - VISUALS
docs.text:
This guide intentionally avoids including texture mods, with a few exceptions. Retextures are highly subjective, and what looks good to me may not suit another. This subjectivity extends to performance as well: opting for high resolution textures across the board may look great, but can significantly impact performance on lower end systems. Additionally, mixing retextures often leads to visual inconsistencies, where untouched objects stand out against retextured ones. For these reasons, textures are best left to personal preference and tailored to your own system.

DUSTy Roads - Expanded ⤓

Compare online or download one or both file(s). To use the downloaded files in MO2:

  1. Click the Open Folders Menu button at the top of the left pane in MO2.
  2. Select Open Profile folder
  3. Move the downloaded files to this folder and overwrite when prompted
  4. Refresh the panes with F5

docs.title: The End...
docs.text:
The journey through this guide is over, but the Mojave Wasteland is still yours to explore. Use what you’ve learned to survive, mod, and shape the DUST experience your way.

Oh yeah, make sure you start the game with New Vegas, and not NVSE!

If you feel confident, you can have a look at the ADDITIONAL MODS section for more content.

If you have any suggestions or complaints, or just want to vent your frustration after being bitten in the ass by Tunnelers again, hop into the DUST Discord server.

docs.title: The Guide
docs.text:
This guide aims to help you set up a stable Fallout New Vegas experience built around DUST Survival Simulator, incorporating stability and performance improvements that have stood the test of time.

What not to expect:

  • Tacticool overhaul;
  • Slooty outfits;
  • Bazillion additional weapons;
  • Ultra-high-resolution textures for every dust speck in the Mojave.

This guide is divided into two paths:

DUSTy Roads - Base

The Base Setup establishes a stable DUST foundation, along with a selection of stability improvements and essential bug fixes. It does not include expansions or additional content, and is intended for those who want to experience the original, yet more stable, version of DUST, or use it as a base for their own mod list.

⮚ DUSTy Roads - Expanded ⮘

The Expanded Setup (and recommended setup) builds on this base, introducing additional mods that enhance gameplay and add extra content, including the major expansions DUST - Expansion Project and DUST - Ink & Ash, both of which are highly recommended! You'll be guided first through the Base setup first, with the option to continue into the Expanded section if you choose to go further.

And if that still isn’t enough, there is also an OPTIONAL SECTION with additional suggestions to further expand your setup, either by complementing the existing mod list or replacing certain installed mods. Keep in mind that inclusion in this section does not necessarily mean the mods are plug-and-play. Some optional mods may require additional patching to resolve balance issues or other conflicts.

docs.title: Using the Guide
docs.text:
Take your time, read the guide in full and avoid skipping steps. If you need support with following the guide, or with your modded game, you can open a support ticket on the DUST Discord (#support-and-bugs-dust), but it’s expected that you’ve followed the instructions carefully and done your due diligence before asking for help. The support page at the end of the guide also includes a modest FAQ covering common issues and questions. Each mod’s requirements and dependencies are accounted for. When a mod lists requirements on its download page, they are either already covered elsewhere in the guide or will be addressed later. Some may be recommendations rather than strict requirements, and may be omitted if not considered necessary. If a required dependency is not already included in the guide, it will be explicitly listed for download at the relevant step. The mod manager of choice is Mod Organizer 2. Though that does not mean you cannot follow the guide as a Vortex user, but you'll have to rely on other sources of information to set up Vortex, or how to install and deploy mods. If you choose to add additional mods, always read their descriptions, instructions, and requirements. You may need to revisit earlier installations to enable compatibility options or install additional patches.

A few mods in this guide are marked with a tag indicating that they:

  • SETTINGS | require a custom INI file that is installed later in the guide (for instance, a custom nvse_stewie_tweaks.ini)
  • DUST PATCH | require a DUST compatibility patch that is installed later in the guide.
  • REINSTALL | require reinstalling a previously installed mod to select additional installer options (primarily used in the Expanded Version).

If this process becomes overwhelming at any point, you can always switch to the WABBAJACK automated installation route.

docs.title: LOD GENERATION
docs.text:
LOD (Level of Detail) refers to simplified versions of distant objects in the game world, such as terrain, buildings, and trees. Instead of rendering full-detail models far away, the game uses lower-detail versions to improve performance. As you move closer, these objects gradually switch to their full-detail versions. Proper LOD ensures distant landscapes look consistent and reduces visual pop-in while keeping the game running smoothly.

  1. Objects LOD: Displays simplified versions of distant structures and objects (like buildings and ruins).
  2. Terrain LOD: Renders the distant landscape (hills, ground, roads) as a lower-detail mesh to create a seamless horizon.
  3. Tree LOD: Primarily used for small flora (bushes, shrubs), while larger trees are often handled by objects LOD.

Why generate LOD if it’s already included in a mod or in this guide? Because LOD is static and does not account for changes made by other mods. By generating LOD yourself, you ensure the visuals accurately reflect your specific mod setup. Dust Community Fixes and Tweaks only includes terrain LOD for the Wasteland, primarily to address water LOD in the drained Colorado River and Lake Mead, but it does not provide object or tree LOD. For that reason, generating LOD yourself is always recommended.

docs.title: Packing LOD in bsa Archives
docs.text:
This step is optional, but strongly recommended. This will positively affect the loading times of LOD assets in-game. There are a few caveats however:

  • bsa archives require a plugin to be loaded. So the name of the archive should equal that of the plugin, with the suffix - Objects and - Terrain
  • Loose files will always override archived files! Check MO2's left pane for conflicts and act accordingly to ensure the right file is conflict winner
  • An .override file is necessary to allow archived files to override other archived files (a JIP LN feature)
Decision When to pack:
  • I want an optimized game and avoid potential stuttering when loading new areas in-game.
  • I am able to resolve asset conflicts and get rid of LOD included in other mods as loose files.
When not to pack:
  • I don’t want to deal with checking file conflicts. Skip to FINISHING TOUCH.

docs.title: MOD ORGANIZER 2
docs.text:
Mod Organizer 2, aka MO2, is a powerful and versatile mod manager, primarily used for Bethesda games. Its standout feature is the virtual file system (USVFS), which keeps mods separate from the actual game folder. This means you can install or remove mods safely, reorder them at any time via drag-and-drop, maintain multiple profiles, and keep your original game files untouched.

MO2’s interface is split into two panes (one for mods, one for plugins) making it easy to spot conflicts and manage load order. Unlike Vortex, which relies on a convoluted group/rules system, MO2 gives you complete control over how mods interact. Additional perks include a fully portable setup, integrated Nexus Mods support for direct downloads, and a plugin system that allows advanced users to extend functionality. While MO2 is generally the superior choice, this doesn’t mean Vortex is a bad mod manager: use whichever tool best fits YOUR needs and comfort level. That said, it is strongly advised to avoid older or unsupported mod managers such as FOMM, NMM (even the Community Edition), Kortex, or Wrye Bash. This also includes MO1.

docs.title: Installing Mod Organizer 2
docs.text:
1. Download the main file (manual download)
  2. Run the installer Mod Organizer 2.exe
  3. When choosing a destination location, pick a location that is not a default Windows directory, not the game folder, not a folder managed by OneDrive, and not inside another portable MO2 installation
  4. When prompted to Select Components, just click Next
  5. You can choose a Start Menu folder and desktop shortcut, or not
  6. Click Install and wait for it to complete
  7. Launch MO2

docs.title: Create an Instance
docs.text:
You will have the option to create either a global instance, or a portable instance. A global instance of MO2 shares settings, profiles, and mods, while a portable instance keeps everything self-contained in a single folder that can be moved or backed up independently. I recommend using a portable instance.

  1. From the game list, select New Vegas
  2. Select the applicable game edition
  3. Choose a name for the instance, e.g. DUSTy Roads
  4. When asked to configure the profile settings, check all boxes
  5. Default location to store data will be under AppData. You can keep this file path, or choose another, but preferably on the same drive as FNV and MO2
  6. Finish and launch the new instance
  7. A pop-up might appear:
    • Show tutorial? Select No
    • Register? Select Yes
    • INI file is read-only? Select Remember my choice in the drop-down and opt for Clear the read-only flag
    • Category setup? Select the option you prefer (I personally don't use the Nexus categories)

docs.title: Game Settings
docs.text:
New Vegas is automatically selected to run (in the top-right corner). But to set a few game settings, change this to Fallout Launcher.

  1. Run the game with Fallout Launcher
  2. Click Options
  3. Select the Ultra preset (or another preset accordingly to your system specifications)
  4. Set the resolution to your monitor's native resolution
  5. Exit the launcher, and change the program back to New Vegas
Information If your resolution is not listed in the launcher, you can set it manually in FalloutPrefs.ini. Click the Tools button in the toolbar.
  1. Select INI Editor
  2. Go to the FalloutPrefs.ini tab
  3. Go to the Display section, and set the following values: iSize W= screen width (e.g., 2560) iSize H= screen height (e.g., 1440)
  4. Click the Save button

Thanks to JIP LN NVSE, you can use a custom INI to add various settings without touching the main INIs. FalloutCustom.ini takes precedence over the other INI files and cannot be modified by the game. Click the Tools button in the toolbar and paste these settings in the FalloutCustom.ini tab:

docs.title: Settings and Workarounds
docs.text:
Click the Settings button in the toolbar to access MO2's settings. There are various settings that let you customize how you interact with MO2, as well as how it looks and feels (Theme tab for example). To keep this guide concise, these options will not be covered, so feel free to explore them yourself. That said, do check these out:

  • Nexus tab: here you can connect/disconnect to Nexus Mods, and associate MO2 with Download with manager links. Here, you can also configure your preferred download server.
  • Workarounds tab: check the option Enable archives parsing (experimental). This will allow MO2 to report conflicts in mod's bsa archives. Useful for troubleshooting!

docs.title: Adding Executables
docs.text:
There are several tools used for modding (such as xEdit and the GECK) or generate LOD (xLODGen). These tools need to be added to MO2 so they can detect and work with your installed mods.

Click the Configuring executables button in the toolbar.
  1. Add an executable by clicking the + button and select Add from file...
  2. Navigate to the location where the tool is installed, and select the executable (.exe or .bat)
  3. You can now give it a name (Title) or add arguments (for instance, -fnv for xEdit)
  4. You can enable additional options based on preference, such as Create files in mod instead of overwrite: here you can specify an output mod for new or modified files

docs.title: Installing Mods
docs.text: To install a mod, first download the mod and locate it in the Downloads tab (right pane). Double-click the downloaded archive to install. Once installed, the mod will appear in the left pane and can be enabled or disabled by ticking its checkbox. The guide will provide any additional instructions when special installation steps are required.

docs.title: Updating Mods
docs.text:
When updating a mod, download the new version and install it the same way as a normal mod. MO2 will detect that a mod with the same name already exists and prompt you to either Replace, Merge, or Rename it.

  • Rename appears when you try to install a file with the same name as an already installed mod. If you're installing an additional or optional file for that mod, rename it accordingly, either by selecting a name from the dropdown or entering one manually. This also simplifies updates when only one of the files needs updating.
  • If you are updating a mod from an older version, select Replace. This will replace all files from the previous version with the new ones.
  • Merge combines the newly downloaded files with the existing mod installation. It's generally best avoided unless you know exactly what you're doing.

In most cases, updates should be installed using the Replace option. However, some updates only contain a few files intended to be added to the existing installation, in which case Rename or Merge could be used instead. Always read the update instructions provided by the mod author, and if you are unsure which option to choose, just ask the author.

docs.title: Left Pane vs Right Pane
docs.text: MO2 uses two panes to manage your modded setup. The left pane controls installed mods and their file priority, determining which mod's assets (textures, meshes, scripts, etc.) take precedence when multiple mods contain the same files. The right pane controls plugin load order, determining the order in which game plugins (.esm and .esp) are loaded. The two panes serve different purposes and should be managed independently. By following the guide's instructions in the order they are presented, mods will be installed with conflicts taken into account. Some conflicts are unavoidable and are handled by the guide's Compatibility Patch. If you decide to add mods outside of the guide, be sure to read Conflict Resolution thoroughly.

docs.title: Overwrite Folder
docs.text: At the bottom of the left pane, you’ll find the Overwrite folder. This folder contains all files generated during gameplay (such as configuration files) or created by modding tools. You can leave these files there, or keep your setup organized by creating a new mod from the Overwrite contents. Keep in mind that files in Overwrite will take priority over other mods, so make sure you know what’s in there and avoid unintentional conflicts. Leaving files unmanaged in Overwrite is one of the most common sources of hidden issues!

docs.title: Conflict Resolution
docs.text:
Just like plugin load order, the mod load order (MO2’s left pane) is equally important. Assets such as textures and meshes are overridden by mods loaded below them (i.e. higher priority). MO2’s Flags column provides visual indicators of file conflicts. Reordering mods (via simple drag and drop) may be necessary to resolve them:

  • means the mod has asset(s) overriding others (conflict winner)
  • means the mod has asset(s) being overridden by others (conflict loser)
  • means the mod has asset(s) both conflict winners as conflict losers
  • When a file in a bsa archive is conflicting, the lightning icon will be blue

To find out what file is conflicting, double-click the mod, and go to the Conflicts tab:

  • Top pane shows the winning file conflicts
  • Middle pane shows the losing file conflicts
  • Bottom pane shows the non-conflicting files

In case of textures (.dds files), MO2 allows you to directly compare the conflicting textures. Double-click the texture to open it in a new window and use the arrow buttons in the top-right corner to cycle through the different versions and decide which one should win the conflict.

Information Rule of thumb: “Lower = wins. Higher = loses.”

To resolve conflicts between plugins (.esm and .esp files), you need a tool like xEdit. On the Resources page you can find further info on the basics of xEdit.

docs.title: PREPARATION
docs.text:
Before deep diving into modding, it’s essential to start with a clean and non-pirated Fallout: New Vegas (FNV) installation and a stable system environment. While the game itself is over 15 years old and its vanilla requirements are modest, a modded setup can place significantly more strain on low-end systems.

As a baseline, you should have at least:

  • 8 GB of RAM,
  • an SSD (strongly recommended),
  • and a CPU and GPU roughly equivalent to a mid-range system from the past decade or newer.
Warning This guide has been developed and tested on Windows. Linux has not been tested or verified by me. Although the guide may work through Proton/Wine, compatibility is not guaranteed, and Linux installations are not supported. Support is provided only for Windows installations that follow this guide.

docs.title: VC++ Redistributables
docs.text:
VC++ Redistributables are runtime libraries published by Microsoft that contain the compiled code for common C++ standard library functions, on which most modding tools rely. By installing the AIO package, you ensure you have the right version installed and won’t encounter crashes on game launch or when using certain modding tools.

  1. Extract the zip-archive
  2. Run the install_all.bat (as administrator)
  3. Restart your PC to complete the installation

docs.title: Disable Base Address Randomization
docs.text:
Base Address Randomization is a Windows security feature that loads executables and DLLs at randomized memory addresses every time a process starts, rather than fixed/predictable ones. Disabling this setting prevents Windows from forcibly randomizing memory addresses for applications that weren’t designed for it, which can otherwise break certain modding hooks.

  1. Open Windows Security
  2. Open App & Browser Control
  3. Open Exploit Protection Settings
  4. Make sure Force randomization for images (Mandatory ASLR) is set to Use default (off)

docs.title: Enable File Extensions
docs.text:
By default, Windows does not display file extensions. File extensions are the suffixes at the end of file names that indicate the file type (such as .exe, .dll, or .esp). These extensions are important when following this guide, so it is highly recommended to enable them.

Windows 11:
  1. Open File Explorer
  2. Open the drop-down menu by clicking View in the menu bar at the top
  3. Under Show, enable File name extensions Windows 10:
    1. Open File Explorer
    2. Go to the View tab
    3. Enable File name extensions

docs.title: Uninstalling FNV
docs.text: A clean installation is strongly recommended to make sure no leftover files from previous modding attempts can cause issues, and to guarantee the game is installed in a safe location. A safe location means avoiding Windows default directories such as Program Files, as well as folders managed by services like OneDrive, which can silently overwrite or restore files. Whether you’re using Steam or GOG, start by uninstalling the game through your library. Then manually delete any remaining files in the installation directory (e.g. steamapps\common\Fallout New Vegas), as well as the Documents\My Games\FalloutNV folder.

docs.title: Installing FNV
docs.text:
Install or reinstall FNV as usual, though make sure to select an installation folder outside any default Windows directories. Instead, install the game in the root of a drive, for example D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Fallout New Vegas, preferably on an SSD, for the best stability and performance. Information The root of a drive is the top-level directory (e.g., C:\) that is not inside any other folder. Steam specific: If your Steam Library is currently located in a default Windows directory (e.g. C:\Program Files (x86), or if you are unsure how to set up a custom library location, you can use the Steam Library Setup Tool ⤓.

  1. Close Steam
  2. Run the downloaded setup tool and add a new entry (Add Row)
  3. Click Accept, confirm when prompted to create a new folder, and exit the tool
  4. Open Steam, install FNV and when asked for install folder, select the newly created library folder

docs.title: Generating INI files
docs.text:
Before setting up a mod manager and installing mods, it’s important to generate fresh INI files. INI files are configuration files that store game settings, which are read by the game on startup. You can do this simply by launching FNV once through Steam or GOG Galaxy. Confirm when prompted to detect video hardware, then exit.

Warning If no pop-ups appear when you run the game, it means the INI files from a previous installation weren’t deleted. Go to Documents\My Games\FalloutNV, delete all INI files, and then try running the game again.

docs.title: RESOURCES
docs.text: The road into modding is long, and not always forgiving. These resources will help you make it through.

docs.title: xEdit
docs.text:
xEdit is a powerful utility for Bethesda games that lets you inspect and modify plugin files. It presents edits in a structured, side-by-side view, making it easy to see how mods interact with each other and with the base game. With xEdit, you can create compatibility patches, analyze what a mod changes, and make your own adjustments where needed. For most use cases, this will be your primary tool for resolving conflicts and creating patches, often without ever needing to open the GECK.

xEdit

You can always find the latest build on the xEdit discord server.

  1. Download the latest build in the #xedit-builds channel
  2. Extract the 7z-archive to a folder on the same drive as FNV and MO2 (and not a default Windows folder!)
  3. Add xFOEdit.exe as an executable to MO2 (see Adding Executables)
  4. Add -fnv in the arguments field

Tome of xEdit

A Comprehensive Guide to using xEdit.

docs.title: GECK
docs.text:
The GECK, or Garden of Eden Creation Kit, is Bethesda’s official editor for FNV, used to create and modify game content. Unlike xEdit’s structured, record-based approach, the GECK provides an environment where you can work with worldspaces, quests, scripts, and other gameplay elements directly. While more powerful, it is also more complex and less suited for quick adjustments. The GECK can be installed from Steam, and it is also bundled with the GOG version.

Warning The GECK is a harsh mistress and often introduces dirty edits. Always clean any modified or newly created plugins with xEdit!

GECK Extender ⤓

The GECK Extender is a project to extend the functionality and fix bugs in the Garden of Eden Creation Kit.

  1. Download the main file Geck manually and place it in the game’s root folder, replacing the original executable
  2. Download the main file Geck Extender and install with MO2 like any other mod
  3. Download the main file GECK Extender - Config and install with MO2 like any other mod

The Unofficial Community GECK Wiki

An unofficial community-run wiki where you'll find everything you need to use The Garden of Eden Creation Kit and make mods for FNV.

docs.text:
Wabbajack is an automated modlist installer. Instead of manually downloading, installing, and configuring hundreds of mods yourself, Wabbajack automates most of the process and reproduces a curated setup as intended by the modlist author. A Wabbajack modlist is built around a predefined collection of mods, configuration files, load orders, patches, and installer settings.

  2. Create a new folder outside of any default Windows folders or the game folder itself, for example: D:\Wabbajack

docs.title: Guide Support
docs.text:
If you get stuck or run into any issues, we’ve got your back. Join our DUST Discord server and navigate to the #support-and-bugs-dust channel. You can make a new post and tag it appropriately. When asking for support, please follow these simple rules:

  • You did some effort to look into the matter yourself.
  • You followed the instructions in the guide AND those of the individual mods.
  • You did not install an ungodly amount of additional mods.
  • You will share your load order, mod list, and crashlog in case of CTDs.
  • Please keep things polite and clear. I work on this in my spare time, and I don't have a lot of it.
Warning A WORD ABOUT NEW VEGAS ANTI CRASH (NVAC) NVAC basically tells the game to not crash, when it wants to crash. So it forces the game to run when it shouldn't. That's not healthy as you can imagine, what may result in an unstable game and even save corruption. NVAC had its merits in the past I guess, but nowadays any scenario where NVAC would stop crashing are fixed by other mods. Except for crashes by broken meshes. But well, why would you want to run a broken mod anyway? Additionally, NVAC can also contribute to crashing due to memory corruption. And when you crash with NVAC active, the crashlog that is generated will be useless. Without reliable crash information, issues cannot be properly diagnosed or fixed. As such, support will not be provided. TL;DR: If your solution is NVAC, your problem isn't solved.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
▼ There's water in Lake Mead and/or Colorado River.

This is usually caused by a load order issue. Either the guide's or your own custom LOD is being overridden by another mod's LOD files, or DUST LOD.esp is not the last plugin in your load order. Check for conflicts in the left pane of MO2 and ensure DUST LOD.esp loads last.

▼ I get notified I miss certain masters: YUP - Base Game + All DLC.esm, DUST - Manan's Tweaks.esp, and DUSTed DUSTesp.

You probably did not install the updated plugin for DUST - Expansion Project (found under Update Files), or it is not placed below the main DUST - Expansion Project installation in MO2. Alternatively, you may have installed a DUST mod that has not been updated for compatibility with DUST Community Fixes and Tweaks.

▼ The game crashes even before reaching the title screen.

Make sure lStewieAl's Tweaks and Engine Fixes is installed and enabled.

▼ Vanilla NPCs appear in DUST.

Another mod is overwriting DUST's NPC changes and requires a compatibility patch.

docs.title: Wabbajack
docs.text:
▼ I installed additional mods, and they are gone after updating the DUSTy Roads Wabbajack.

You did not add the [NoDelete] prefix to their names in the left pane, as instructed on the Wabbajack page.

▼ Can I update whenever there's an update?

Consult the changelog first to find out whether it is safe to update mid-game. If it isn't, this will be stated explicitly. If in doubt, don't hesitate to ask!

Wabbajack is an automated modlist installer. Instead of manually downloading, installing, and configuring hundreds of mods yourself, Wabbajack automates most of the process and reproduces a curated setup as intended by the modlist author. A Wabbajack modlist is built around a predefined collection of mods, configuration files, load orders, patches, and installer settings. For the user, the process is straightforward: after installing the required tools and selecting a modlist, Wabbajack automatically downloads the necessary files from sources such as Nexus Mods and configures the setup with minimal manual interaction. Once completed, you receive a ready-to-play modded installation. If you'd like to learn more about Wabbajack, check out the Wabbajack Wiki. The DUSTy Roads Wabbajack provides two profiles:

  • a Base Version featuring DUST, and essential fixes,
  • and an Expanded Version that further builds upon this foundation with additional gameplay enhancements and content, such as Expansion Project, Ink & Ash, and more.
You can consult the mod lists on Load Order Library for a complete overview of the included mods: DUSTy Roads - Base | DUSTy Roads - Expanded. Alternatively, you can browse through the sections of the guide.

Warning This Wabbajack has been developed and tested on Windows. Linux has not been tested or verified by me. Although it may work through Proton/Wine, compatibility is not guaranteed, and Linux installations are not supported. Support is provided only for Windows installations.

docs.title: Pre-Installation
docs.text: Prior to starting the automated installation, a few manual steps are required to prepare your system, including installing the game and downloading Wabbajack.

docs.text: It is essential to read and complete the Preparation section of the guide before proceeding with the Wabbajack installation!

docs.title: DUSTy Roads Wabbajack
docs.text:
Until DUSTy Roads is approved and added to the Wabbajack UI, it can only be installed from disk by first downloading the .wabbajack file.

docs.title: Wabbajack
docs.text:
1. Download the installer using the Download Now button
  2. Create a new folder outside of any default Windows folders or the game folder itself, for example: D:\Wabbajack
  3. Move the downloaded Wabbajack.exe into this new folder

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Double-click the downloaded DUSTy Roads.wabbajack file
  2. On the left side, set both the Installation Location and the Downloads Location. These folders cannot be:
    • the game folder,
    • a default Windows folder,
    • the Wabbajack folder,
    • or another folder already containing a MO2 installation.
    Example of a suitable location: D:\Mod Lists\DUSTy Roads
  3. Click the Install button and log in to Nexus Mods when prompted
  4. Authorize Wabbajack, then simply wait for the downloads and installation to finish...
  5. When finished, click the Open in File Explorer button to open the folder where the mod list is installed
Information If you do not have a Premium account, you will need to manually confirm each mod download. The time required to download and install everything depends on your Nexus Mods account type and internet speed.

  1. In the installation folder of the DUSTy Roads Wabbajack, open the _Manual Install folder
  2. Copy everything from this folder to the game's root folder:
    • xNVSE files
    • FNV BSA Decompressor files
    • FNV 4GB Patcher executable
Information The root folder is the main directory where the game is installed; the directory containing FalloutNV.exe.

docs.title: Mod Organizer 2 Setup
docs.text:
1. Launch ModOrganizer.exe from the DUSTy Roads installation folder
  2. A Register? pop-up might appear: Select Yes
  3. Run the game with the Fallout Launcher, not New Vegas
  4. Click Options
  5. Select the Ultra preset (or another preset accordingly to your system specifications)
  6. Set the resolution to your monitor's native resolution
  7. Exit the launcher, and change the program back to New Vegas
Information If your resolution is not listed in the launcher, you can set it manually in FalloutPrefs.ini. Click the Tools button in the toolbar.
  1. Select INI Editor
  2. Go to the FalloutPrefs.ini tab
  3. Go to the Display section, and set the following values: iSize W= screen width (e.g., 2560) iSize H= screen height (e.g., 1440)
  4. Click the Save button

docs.title: Finish
docs.text:
Done. That's it. Your descent into cannibalism can now begin. Select the appropriate profile from the drop-down menu at the top of the left pane:

  • DUSTy Roads - Base: featuring DUST and essential fixes.
  • DUSTy Roads - Expanded: base version with major expansions and additional gameplay enhancements.

And make sure New Vegas is selected in the Run drop-down menu, not NVSE!

docs.title: How to Update?
docs.text:
Each time a new update is released, the following steps are required:

  1. Before updating, always consult the changelog for details on new additions, removals, fixes, and any manual update instructions. Existing saves are generally compatible unless noted otherwise.
  2. Launch Wabbajack and use the same installation folder as the existing mod list installation.
Warning If you added any mods after the installation, add the [NoDelete] prefix to their names in the left pane. Keep in mind that these mods may still be moved or disabled after updating the mod list.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
If you get stuck or run into any issues, we’ve got your back. Join our DUST Discord server and navigate to the #support-and-bugs-dust channel. You can make a new post and tag it appropriately. When asking for support, please follow these simple rules:

  • You did some effort to look into the matter yourself.
  • You followed the installation instructions.
  • You did not install an ungodly amount of additional mods.
  • You will share your load order, and mod list (and crashlog in case of CTDs).
  • Please keep things polite and clear. I work on this in my spare time, and I don't have a lot of it.

You can also check the guide's FAQ for solutions to common issues.

Information Copy-paste from Wabbajack: "Do not contact mod or guide authors for support. If you use a Wabbajack modlist, only go to that list's curator for support on any issues you may have." Warning A WORD ABOUT NEW VEGAS ANTI CRASH (NVAC) NVAC basically tells the game to not crash, when it wants to crash. So it forces the game to run when it shouldn't. That's not healthy as you can imagine, what may result in an unstable game and even save corruption. NVAC had its merits in the past I guess, but nowadays any scenario where NVAC would stop crashing are fixed by other mods. Except for crashes by broken meshes. But well, why would you want to run a broken mod anyway? Additionally, NVAC can also contribute to crashing due to memory corruption. And when you crash with NVAC active, the crashlog that is generated will be useless. Without reliable crash information, issues cannot be properly diagnosed or fixed. As such, support will not be provided. TL;DR: If your solution is NVAC, your problem isn't solved.

If you're confident enough to get your hands dirty, you can have a look at the ADDITIONAL MODS section for more content.
